propositions: Multiple bundle objects for a single ref cause git ls-remote to return ambiguous heads and fresh clones to fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', rendering the store unclonable; git-remote-s3's cmd_push rejects all writes while bundles>1, stalling the push path and preventing retry convergence.

Upstream's Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() prompts that crash on EOF) and discards non-chosen heads to orphan refs, losing events unique to those heads and violating the append-only log contract; rebar's store must losslessly merge divergent heads, never discard.

The heal must acquire the helper's per-ref lock (acquire_lock/release_lock) to serialize cross-clone repairs, re-enumerate bundles under the lock to guard against TOCTOU, fetch each bundle's divergent head locally, fold all heads via iterated 2-parent merges (following sync's existing lossless reconcile semantics with --allow-unrelated-histories for unrelated-history heads), and write the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting any originals to ensure ≥1 bundle carries the full merged history at every crash point.

The heal must run the local git merge under rebar's write_lock (the same lock sync.reconverge and push_tickets_branch take) so it cannot race concurrent local committers; lock ordering is cycle-free (helper S3 lock outer, rebar write_lock inner) so at most one doctor ever reaches the merge.

On a genuine content conflict (non-derived file divergently edited), the heal must abort, delete no remote bundles, release the lock, and surface rebar fsck-recover rather than silently discarding a parent; multi-process contention (N processes hitting the multi-bundle state) serializes via the helper lock so exactly one doctor merges and the rest back off, converging on the winner's collapsed remote.

push_tickets_branch must detect the multi-bundle signature in stderr (_is_multi_bundle predicate matching 'multiple bundles exists on server' or 'multiple updates for ref'), branch to heal_multi_bundle at the non-FF seam guarded by a healed_once flag (capping this push call at one heal attempt to prevent thrash), and retry the push; all S3 access routes through a single adapter that imports S3Remote/parse_git_url lazily behind require_s3_helper(), adding no direct boto3 or credential dependency to core rebar.
